name: John Armstrong to James Madison, Paris, 20 February 1808 (unique code + shorthand)
ciphertext_source: Founders Online, Papers of James Madison, Secretary of State Series, document 99-01-02-2728 ("To James Madison from John Armstrong, Jr., 20 February 1808"); NARA RG 59, Despatches from United States Ministers to France, microcopy M34 roll 14, images 29-32. Transcription copied unmodified from Daniel Bourdeau's cyphersolver repository (github.com/dbourdeau/cyphersolver, armstrong/feb20_ciphertext.txt, commit 763a3b98ab1c; MIT code / CC BY 4.0 text, CLAUDE.md rule 8), itself read from the Founders Online Wayback copy (founders.archives.gov itself answers scripted fetches with an empty HTTP 202 CloudFront challenge, confirmed 26 Sept 2026).
alphabet: numeral groups (integers 1 to 1900) plus 35 short passages and 2 full lines of graphic symbols resembling a period shorthand, unclassified

constraints.not_the_office_code: not Armstrong's routine THE=972 code used with Madison 1804-1810: Bourdeau's own paired check decodes the 15 Feb 1808 Armstrong-to-Madison letter (5 days earlier, same code) at 72% coherent, but this letter at only 25% and those hits are noise -- 'the 20 Feb code is a different code' (ciphers/armstrong-madison-1808/NOTES.md, 'What the cipher is'). Madison himself wrote to Jefferson, 15 May 1808 (Founders 99-01-02-3082), that 'No such Cypher is in the office, and must be one concerted with another correspondent'.
constraints.shorthand_passages: 35 short + 2 full-line passages in graphic symbols, not numerals; Tomokiyo compared them to Taylor's 1786 shorthand (no match) and lists Weston/Mitchell/Gurney/Byrom/Mavor/Macaulay as untested period alternatives (per a Norbert Biermann bibliography lead, a German 1895 book pp.38-40)
constraints.sibling_codes: THE=972 (Armstrong<->Madison, ~1600 elements, 580 published in part by Bourdeau as key972.js, does not fit this letter); WE027 (Livingston<->Madison, ~1700 elements, named by Tomokiyo but not published anywhere found, only cited to Weber 1979 pp.154/188); WE028 (Monroe<->Madison, 1600 elements, THE=1385, fully published by Tomokiyo as WE028.txt) -- same office/period/construction convention (word-and-syllable groups, blockwise-alphabetical runs, common-word homophones), no sibling's own values shown to fit this letter
constraints.afio_claim_rejected: AFIO's 27 May 2025 announcement of a Yaacov Apelbaum decryption (56-entry key, 60-word plaintext) is rejected by both Tomokiyo (qualitative, Oct 2025/June 2026) and Bourdeau (quantitative, 16 Sept 2026): the key covers only 133/369 groups (36%), and a key built by the same construction procedure on a SHUFFLED copy of the ciphertext fits the claimed plaintext better than the real key does (500-key control: 70%/41% vs the AFIO key's 59%/30% on two occurrence-consistency measures) -- a matched-control negative already run and on file, not to be re-run as a 'first' test here.
constraints.queue_row_27_test_needs_correction: QUEUE.md row 27's own named cheap test ('Place Krajcovic's crib from Armstrong's 15 Feb 1808 letter to Jefferson...') has two errors found this intake: the 15 Feb 1808 letter is TO MADISON, not Jefferson (Founders 99-01-02-2703, confirmed by direct fetch); and no 'Krajcovic' connects to Armstrong or this letter anywhere reached -- the only Krajcovic on file in this repository is a solver credited on the unrelated catokwacopa-1875 target (UNSOLVED-SURVEY.md line 113). cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Crib/vocabulary placement: take Armstrong's other 1808 letters already in clear or already decoded (15 Feb 1808 to Madison, Founders 99-01-02-2703, THE=972, ~72% coherent per Bourdeau; 22 Feb 1808 to Madison, Founders 99-01-02-2733, also THE=972) as a period/register/idiolect crib -- word-length distribution, common-word frequency ranks, repeat-group spacing -- and place it against this letter's opening groups and its 216-distinct-value profile. Matched control: the same placement test run against a synthetic 369-group sequence built from THE=972's own group-value distribution (same alphabet size, same design: word/syllable code, blockwise-alphabetical). Report both numbers (CLAUDE.md rule 3). Cost $2-3, Sonnet.

2. Sibling-code vocabulary transfer (Tomokiyo's suggestion): test whether WE028's full 1600-entry table (Monroe's code, same office/period/construction convention, published in full) transfers ANY values to this letter's 216 distinct groups above chance -- i.e. whether shared group numbers across the two codes agree on word/syllable more often than a random pairing of two same-sized blockwise-alphabetical codebooks would. Matched control: WE028 against a size-and-structure-matched synthetic code built the same way THE=972 was shown not to fit (shuffle WE028's own value assignments, keep the alphabetical-block structure). Only run if test 1 does not already close the target. Cost $2-3, Sonnet.

3. Shorthand identification: compare the 35+2 graphic-symbol passages against period shorthand systems named by Tomokiyo (Weston 1727/1730/1788, Mitchell 1760, Gurney 1750, Byrom 1739, Mavor 1780, Macaulay 1747, Taylor 1786) using period specimen images (Google Books). Cost $2, Sonnet, needs specimen images fetched first.
matched_control: test 1's and test 2's own controls are named per-test above (rule 3: design-matched, not just length/alphabet-matched, since this letter's own design -- a code Bourdeau's own paired check shows is NOT THE=972 -- has no independently-solved sibling of the same design at this length on file yet)

judge.corpora_note: Built and fold-checked 26 Sept 2026 (LANE ARM ARM-EN18, tools/data/en18/README.md): 1795-1815 American diplomatic/official English (Monroe Vols II/V, Gallatin Vol I, Madison Vols VII/VIII, Jefferson Vol IX), 4,806,387 letters folded. Leave-one-file-out at N=1000/1500 (about this target's own 369-code decode length): blended false-negative rate 14.2%/15.1%, per-fold spread 0.270/0.260 -- roughly 4x lower blended rate and 2.5x tighter spread than the same check on LANG_CORPORA['en'] at the same N (58.6%/64.8% blended, 0.675/0.710 spread). Still above the EN-FOLDS amendment's 0.05 per-fold-spread gate (driven by Gallatin Vol I and Jefferson Vol IX reading as outliers against the more despatch-heavy Monroe/Madison volumes): treat a judge FAIL or PASS on this target as substantially better-calibrated than under 'en' but still of a known, non-zero residual unreliability, not a settled result.
